paragraphs: The GLC43 AMG has been part of the GLC-Class range since 2015, and across its two generations has used two different engines — from the M276 V6 through to today's M139 4-cylinder hybrid. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLC43 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre V6 petrol fitted to the GLC43 AMG from 2015 to 2022 (X253 generation). No specific known issue confirmed for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other GLC43 AMG rebuilds.

A 2.0-litre I4 hybrid petrol fitted to the GLC43 AMG from 2022 to present (X254 generation). This is a notable departure from the older V6, part of a wider AMG shift to hybridised 4-cylinder power. No specific known issue confirmed for this application — it's a newer engine and we treat it as such.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLC43 AMG spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M276 part will work on an M139 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLC-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
